title: Artin theorem for an embedded join of henselizations
statement: Let $P$ be a normal integral domain [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring], let $K=\operatorname{Frac}(P)$, and fix a separable closure $K^{\mathrm{sep}}/K$ [def-kun-separably-closed]. For prime ideals $\mathfrak q_1,\mathfrak q_2\subset P$, choose $P$-embeddings $P^h_{\mathfrak q_i}\hookrightarrow K^{\mathrm{sep}}$ of their ordinary henselizations [def-weil-pbc-henselization-at-prime]. Let $J$ be the subring of $K^{\mathrm{sep}}$ generated by their images. Then $J$ is a henselian local ring [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology]. If neither $\mathfrak q_1\subseteq\mathfrak q_2$ nor $\mathfrak q_2\subseteq\mathfrak q_1$, then $J$ is strictly henselian and the contraction to $P$ of its maximal ideal is strictly contained in both $\mathfrak q_i$.

source.place: Theorem 6.1, printed p. 12, citing Artin, On the joins of Hensel rings, Theorems 2.2 and 2.5. Online Huebner--Schmidt paper read; local archival copy and the original Artin paper WANTED.
